label: Review of Smooth Manifolds
notes: This appendix, spanning printed pages 371 through 390, refreshes the smooth-manifold prerequisites the Riemannian theory rests on. We move from topological manifolds and charts to tangent vectors, differentials, vector fields, the Lie bracket, submanifolds, and flows, fixing the notation used throughout the main text.

label: Topological Manifolds
notes: A topological manifold is locally like Euclidean space yet globally curved. We require Hausdorff and second countable so that pathologies like the line with two origins are excluded and partitions of unity exist, which later makes global Riemannian metrics possible by patching local data together.

label: Charts and Atlases
notes: A chart gives coordinates near a point, and an atlas covers the manifold with such charts. Where two charts overlap, the transition map records how the coordinate systems disagree. Compatibility of these transitions is exactly what upgrades a bare topological manifold into a smooth one.

label: Smooth Structures
notes: A smooth atlas has all transition maps infinitely differentiable, and a maximal such atlas is a smooth structure. Smoothness is intrinsic: it never depends on a particular chart, only on whether overlaps are compatible. This frees every later construction from the accident of chosen coordinates.

label: Smooth Maps and Diffeomorphisms
notes: A map between manifolds is smooth when it looks smooth in every coordinate representation. A diffeomorphism is a smooth bijection with smooth inverse, the natural notion of equivalence here. Two diffeomorphic manifolds are indistinguishable as smooth objects, so we classify manifolds up to diffeomorphism.

label: Tangent Vectors
notes: A tangent vector at a point is a derivation: a linear map on smooth germs obeying the product rule. The coordinate partials form a basis, so the tangent space is a vector space of the manifold's dimension. This algebraic definition needs no ambient space to host the manifold.

label: The Tangent Space
notes: Each point carries its own tangent space, a flat linear approximation of the manifold there. Curves through the point give velocity vectors, and every tangent vector arises this way. Assembling all tangent spaces produces the tangent bundle, the natural arena for vector fields and dynamics.

label: The Differential and Pushforward
notes: A smooth map's differential linearly sends tangent vectors forward, turning the velocity of a curve into the velocity of its image. In coordinates the differential is the Jacobian matrix. This pushforward is the chain rule made geometric, and it underlies immersions, submersions, and rank conditions.

label: Vector Fields
notes: A vector field smoothly assigns a tangent vector to each point, a section of the tangent bundle. Equivalently it is a derivation of the algebra of smooth functions. In a chart it becomes a first-order differential operator whose coefficient functions vary smoothly across the manifold.

label: The Lie Bracket
notes: The Lie bracket of two vector fields measures their failure to commute as flows. It is again a vector field, antisymmetric and satisfying the Jacobi identity, making vector fields a Lie algebra. Vanishing bracket means the flows commute and local coordinates can straighten both fields simultaneously.

label: Submanifolds and the Rank Theorem
notes: Immersions have injective differential; embeddings are immersions that are also topological embeddings, yielding embedded submanifolds. The constant rank theorem normalizes any constant-rank map to a linear projection in suitable coordinates, explaining why level sets of submersions are smooth submanifolds of predictable dimension.

label: Flows of Vector Fields
notes: Integrating a vector field produces its flow, a one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms whose orbits are the field's integral curves. The fundamental theorem guarantees existence and uniqueness locally. Flows convert infinitesimal data into finite motion and define the Lie derivative measuring change along the field.

label: Synthesis
notes: The appendix builds one tower: topology supports charts, charts support smoothness, smoothness supports tangent vectors and differentials, and these support fields, brackets, submanifolds, and flows. With this scaffolding fixed, the main text can add a metric and develop genuinely Riemannian geometry on solid ground.
